doc.title: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan Jaffe, Sandra Jaffe Interview, 1961-11-25
doc.interviewee: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan Jaffe, Sandra Jaffe

title: Sandra Jaffe on coming from Philadelphia and seeing the Eureka band
summary: The Jaffes came from Philadelphia expecting to hear the music, found the bands idle, and followed the Eureka to the Cabildo.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How'd you get the idea to come down here and start this New Orleans revival of jazz or work with it? Well, we didn't come down here for that specific purpose. We came down from Philadelphia in about April and thought we'd be hearing a lot of these musicians and a lot of this music. And we didn't. We knew a lot of these men were still alive, that bands like the Eureka and Young Tuxedo Brass bands were still organized, and they were not playing anywhere. The first time that we saw them was about a month later. We saw Eureka hats and instruments walking down the street, so we followed them to the museum on Jackson Square, the Cabildo. And there the Eureka played for the Friends of the Cabildo, which was a humorous sight. All the Dowagers and friends and people sitting there. And the first few blasts of the horns, I thought the ceiling would fall in and the floor would open and the paintings of all the portraits of the ancestors would come off the walls. But they had the crowd swinging after a while. Well, so, but you must have known something about jazz. Well, Alan was a big jazz fan, and I knew a little bit about it, but I wasn't that involved in Philadelphia. But I did like it very much, and I did expect to hear a lot of it down here. But at this time, I had no sort of attachment to any of these men. I knew nothing about their status down here or anything about their not playing down here. And once coming down here, I became more sympathetic to the situation, which eventually evolved in our starting across the street. Well, Alan, let me ask you how you found these men. I mean, you didn't just wander freely around and say, do you play an instrument?
